scope: Four visual directions each for idle, forward walk, backward walk, backdash, and run. Four drawn key poses per option; not registered, timed production animation.
user_brief: Give me 4 versions of an idle pose, walk, back walk, back dash, and run cycle. For the idle I was imagining him tapping his hook handle on his shoulder and looking down on the opponent.
design_rules: Current F / Shoulder Rest identity, low-volume long white hair and physical cobalt sports glasses.
Wooden hook-handle tap on shoulder; hooked blade kept clear of body. Downward glance at opponent.
Opposed hips and shoulders, soft knees, heel articulation and clear load/release from approved Low Scoop study.
One right-hand hooked pole and one left-hand short triangular knife; no body smears.
Facing right during all studies. Forward movements travel right; retreats travel left.
A-D are independent options on each sheet; choices can be mixed.
pixel_processing: Generated PNGs copied byte-for-byte; no crop, paint, filter, warp, rescale or compositing.
production_follow_up: After selection, make clean individually registered cycle frames with measured fixed weapon dimensions.
Resolve any concept-sheet foreshortening and verify alternating leg identity and planted contacts during timed playback.
Set loop timing, holds, foot roots and secondary-motion offsets after selecting movement character; these boards do not change gameplay speed, reach or invulnerability.

jobs.title: SHARK / IDLE OPTIONS
jobs.prompt:
Create a polished ANIMATION DIRECTION COMPARISON SHEET for SHARK, the exact original Fight Guild fighter in the supplied references. This is a visual options study for a fighting game, with real drawn movement progression. Reference 1 locks his design and fixed weapon geometry. Reference 2 is his approved F / Shoulder Rest neutral. Reference 3 shows the approved fluid acting, torso twist, grounded weight shifts and articulated ankles: match that quality, not stiff mannequin posing.

LAYOUT: large portrait illustration approximately 1536 x 2048. Exactly FOUR horizontal option rows A, B, C, D. FOUR chronological full-body key poses in each row: 16 drawings total, no extra character portraits. Give each row its own pale ivory horizontal band and a narrow dark-teal title strip with its option letter and short name; four spacious equal columns beneath it. Clear small 01,02,03,04 over each pose. Thin quiet separators. All figures rendered at identical anatomical scale, NOT normalized to bounding boxes; leave enough room for the entire pole, hook, hair and boots. Clean ivory background with sparse charcoal typography and teal accents, very faint ground guide only. No stage, no opponent, no decorations, no water or attack effects. Broad readable silhouettes and clean negative space matter more than costume microdetail.

CHARACTER LOCK: mature tall athletic swimmer, eight-head anatomy, broad shoulders and narrow waist, long muscular legs, small angular adult face. LONG WHITE HAIR with low crown and slim locks following his nape/back, no gigantic mane, no ponytail. Physical COBALT BLUE SPORTS GLASSES (bridge, lenses, arms), natural skin, no face paint. Sleeveless teal scale vest, bone shark-jaw armor on anatomical LEFT shoulder, leather bracers, rope waist belt with hip net, torn teal sash, slate loose trousers, brown strapped heavy boots. RIGHT hand holds ONE continuous rope-wrapped wooden pole with a SINGLE OPEN SILVER J-HOOK at one end and small ring at butt; left hand holds his separate short triangular knife, pointed safely away from body. Fixed weapon dimensions across all poses, total hooked shaft about 0.9 of standing body height, no added spear point, no second hook. Exactly two arms, two legs, one right-hand hook, one left-hand knife. The hook MUST remain supported by his right hand; no floating or disappearing weapon.

RENDER: confident anime fighting-game animation key drawings, thick dark outer ink, finer interiors, strong two-value cel shadows, restrained upper-left light. All poses face screen RIGHT with the opponent imagined to the right; keep eyes directed toward that opponent, never turn the whole character left. Three-quarter SIDE GAMEPLAY CAMERA, no foreshortened camera tricks. Pose through the hips, ribcage and shoulder opposition, flexed feet, clear heel pivots and knees. Allow compression, extension, delayed hair/sash settling. No body/weapon smears, no stretched rubber limbs, no duplicate limbs, no speed streaks. Do not just rotate a rigid torso or repeat identical legs. Anatomical size consistency MUST NOT suppress posture changes. Four keys must show a real connected action in every row.

TITLE: SHARK / IDLE OPTIONS
All FOUR options follow the user's specific idea: Shark taps the ROPE-WRAPPED WOODEN HANDLE of his hook on his RIGHT SHOULDER and looks down his nose at his opponent. The METAL HOOK stays safely behind him on screen left; he does NOT hit himself with the sharp end. Right hand loosely lifts the supported shaft a few centimeters then lets its wrapped section touch the shoulder, with a visible settling response in chest/shoulder. Left-hand short knife hangs low and idle, never waves across his body. Eyes angled down through his blue glasses while chin carries a superior attitude.
A / LAZY TAP: relaxed tall rear-leg-weighted stagger, chest open, front knee loose. 01 shoulder rest, 02 wrist lifts handle while ribcage inhales and head inclines down, 03 soft shoulder tap with slight clavicle dip, 04 long relaxed settle with a small smirk. Single unhurried beat.
B / DOUBLE BEAT: looser asymmetric stance and rolling shoulders, knees soft, rhythm through hip sway. 01 left-hip settle and handle raised, 02 first shoulder contact, 03 tiny rebound and weight shift toward center, 04 second tap and amused downward glance. Distinct springy double-tap mannerism; the last pose easily flows into first.
C / LOOMING: wider planted base, torso slightly inclined toward opponent, head low but gaze condescending. 01 compressed right hip, 02 rear leg slowly extends to raise the chest above opponent with handle lifted, 03 deliberate tap and forward ribcage settle, 04 return into lower hip with shoulder still relaxed. A dangerous measured weight shift, no attack windup.
D / SIDE-EYE: most theatrical S-curve: hips forward, ribcage leaned back, hooked pole relaxed over rear shoulder, leading boot toe cocked. 01 chin up, 02 head turns a few degrees down toward opponent while handle lifts, 03 dismissive tap with wrist drop and shoulder bounce, 04 head canted with half-smile and toe returning. Still combat-ready, not a dance or caricature.
Make neck/head/wrist differences legible, with nuanced whole-body support, not four copies of one pose. Small curved arrows at handle and shoulder are allowed to clarify the tap, but no cartoon impact star.

TITLE: SHARK / BACKWARD WALK

D / TOE-ROLL RETREAT: relaxed upper back leans slightly away from opponent, lively calf/ankle articulation, leading knee soft and rear foot feeling for ground. TITLE: SHARK / BACKDASH
Four distinct finite BACKDASH animations, not a forward dash or looping walk. Shark keeps face and attention RIGHT while escaping LEFT.
